question.text:
$\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ start from the same point. $\text{A}$ walks $35 \mathrm{~m}$ South, then turns West and walks $15 \mathrm{~m}$, then turns to his right and walks $45 \mathrm{~m}$. At the same time, $\text{B}$ walks $25 \mathrm{~m}$ North, then turns to his left and walks $15 \mathrm{~m}$. Where is $\text{B}$ now with respect to the position of $\text{A}.$

  1. $\text{B}$ is $95 \mathrm{~m}$ to the North of $\text{A}$
  2. $\text{B}$ is $15 \mathrm{~m}$ to the South of $\text{A}$
  3. $\text{B}$ is $15 \mathrm{~m}$ to the North of $\text{A}$
  4. $\text{B}$ is $95 \mathrm{~m}$ to the South of $\text{A}$

$\text{“A"}$ can do a work in $12$ days and $\text{“B"}$ can do the same work in $24$ days. If they work on it together for $4$ days, then what fraction of work is left?

  1. $1 / 2$
  2. $1 / 4$
  3. $1 / 3$
  4. $1 / 5$

What is the average of numbers from $1$ to $50$ which are multiple of $2$ or $5 ?$

  1. $25.4$
  2. $25.9$
  3. $26.4$
  4. $25.8$

The ratio of monthly income of $\text{A} \& \text{B}$ is $4: 5$ And that of their monthly Expenditure is $3: 8$. If the income of $A$ is equal to the Expenditure of $\text{B},$ then what is the ratio of savings of $\text{A} \& \text{B}.$

  1. $2: 5$
  2. $5: 2$
  3. $8: 3$
  4. $5: 4$

• $\text{A@B}$ means $\text{‘A is the mother of B’}$
  • $\text{A#B}$ means $\text{‘A is the sister of B’}$
  • $\text{A?B}$ means $\text{‘A is the daughter of B’}$

Which of the following expressions means  $\text{‘}x$ is the daughter of $y\text{’}?$

  1. $y@z?x\#w$
  2. $y@z\#x?w$
  3. $w@z?x\#y$
  4. $w@x?z\#y$

If a solid metal square prism whose base perimetre is $36 \mathrm{~cm}$ and height $9 \mathrm{~cm}$ is melted and forms a closed hollow pyramid(negligible thickness) with a square base of side $3 \mathrm{~cm}$. What would be the slant height of the lateral surface of the pyramid?
  1. $3 \mathrm{~cm}$
  2. $12 \mathrm{~cm}$
  3. $81 \mathrm{~cm}$
  4. $72 \mathrm{~cm}$

The quantities $\text{S}$ and $\text{T}$ are positive and are related by the equation $\text{S}=\frac{k}{T}$, where $k$ is a constant. If the value of $\text{S}$ increases by $50$ percent, then the value of $\text{T}$ decreases by what percent?

  1. $25 \%$
  2. $33 \frac{1}{3} \%$
  3. $50 \%$
  4. $66 \frac{2}{3} \%$

Which of the following functions $f$ defined for all numbers $x$ has the property that $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for all numbers $x?$
  1. $f(x)=\frac{x^3}{x^2+1}$
  2. $f(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x^2+1}$
  3. $f(x)=x^2\left(x^2-1\right)$
  4. $f(x)=x\left(x^3-1\right)$

If a $\textsf{SIX}$ digit number $5 z 3 x 4 y$ is divisible by $7,11,13$. Then what is the value of $(x+y-z)?$

  1. 3
  2. 4
  3. 5
  4. 6

Fill the most appropriate phrase in the blank out of the given options.
Nothing _____ like seeing these cyclists run every red light in town.
  1. buy a pig in a poke
  2. blow my own trumpet
  3. sets my teeth on edge
  4. blunt the edge

\overset{\textbf{R}}{\begin{array}{|cc|} \hline \mathrm{A} & \mathrm{B} \\

3 & 2 \\
5 & 6 \\

9 & 8 \\

What is the number of tuples in the result of the following relational algebra query:
$$
\pi_{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{R} \bowtie \mathbf{T}) \bowtie \pi_{\mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}}(\mathbf{S} \bowtie \mathbf{T}) ?
$$

A decimal number $\text{“A"}$ is represented in $2\text{'s}$ complement binary form as $a_n a_{n-1} \ldots a_0.$
Which of the following correctly represents $\text{“A"}?$

  1. $\text{A}=-2^{n-1} a_n+\sum_{i=0}^{n-2} 2^i a_i$
  2. $\text{A}=-2^n a_n+\sum_{i=0}^n 2^i a_i$
  3. $\text{A}=-2^n a_n+\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} 2^i a_i$
  4. $\text{A}=-2^{n-1} a_{n-1}+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} 2^i a_i$

Consider a following recursive function $\textsf{f()}.$

#include<stdio.h>
int f(int *a, int n)
{
    if(n <= 0) return 0;
    if(*a % 2 == 0)
        return *a + f(a+1, n-1);
    else
        return *a -f(a+1, n-1);
}


Let array a contain numbers from $1$ to $10$ then what will be the output $\textsf{f(a,10)}?$

  1. $-1$
  2. $11$
  3. $9$
  4. None of these

Consider the following task graph and given task lengths (in time units). The unspecified $x$ and $y$ are non-negative numbers.

Each edge $\mathrm{Ti} \rightarrow \mathrm{Tj}$ shows that we can not execute task $\mathrm{Tj}$ before $\mathrm{Ti}$.
Suppose the workload is executed in a task-parallel manner for the lowest possible completion time on $3$ CPUs. What is the total earliest time for $x=10$ and $y=20$ such that all tasks finished successfully?

We are allowed to schedule any task to any CPU to optimise the total time.

  1. $50$
  2. $55$
  3. $45$
  4. $35$

A binary tree $\text{T}$ is full if either $\text{T}$ has one node, or the root of $\text{T}$ has two children which are roots of full binary trees. For instance, a full binary tree with depth $2$ has one of the following three shapes:

Let $s_n$ be the total number of shapes of full binary trees with depth $n$. From the previous picture, we see that $s_2=3$. Also, it is easy to see that $s_0=s_1=1$. Which of the following recursive formulas holds for all $n \geq 3:$

  1. $2 \cdot s_{n-1} \sum_{k=0}^{n-2} s_k+s_{n-1}^2$
  2. $2 \cdot s_{n-1} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} s_k$
  3. $s_{n-1}+s_{n-2}$
  4. $s_{n-1} \cdot s_{n-2}$

Consider the following grammar:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{S} \rightarrow & \text{S} \text { and } \text{S} \\
\mid & \text{S} \text { or } \text{S} \\
\mid & \text{T} \\
\mid & \text { a } \\
\text{T} \rightarrow & \text { a }
\end{aligned}
$$
In this grammar $\text{S}$ and $\text{T}$ are the non-terminals and $\text{S}$ is the start symbol$\text{; "and", "or", }$and $\text{"a"}$ are terminal symbols.
How many parse trees are there for the string: "$\mathrm{a \;and} \;\text{a or a}$"

Which of the following are $f(n)=n^{\Theta(1)}?$ 

  1. $f(n)=3 n^3+17 n^2+4$.
  2. $f(n)=3 n^3 \log n$
  3. $f(n)=n^{3 \log n}$
  4. $f(n)=3 \log n$

Let $\text{L}$ be a language consisting of finitely many strings. Hence, $\text{L}$ is regular and, therefore, context-free.

Let $k$ be the maximum length of any string in $\text{L}$.

Which of the following is true for the context-free grammars that generate $\text{L}?$

  1. Every context-free grammar in Chomsky's normal form that generates $\text{L}$ has more than $\log (k)$ variables. (The logarithm is in base $2.)$
  2. Some context-free grammar in Chomsky’s normal form that generates $\text{L}$ has less than $\log (k)$ variables. (The logarithm is in base $2.)$
  3. Every context-free grammar in Chomsky’s normal form that generates $\mathrm{L}$ has exactly $2 k-1$ variables.
  4. There is a context-free grammar in Chomsky's normal form that generates $\mathrm{L}$ and that has only one variable.

Which of the following rules about functional dependencies is valid?

  1. If $\alpha \rightarrow \beta$ and $\gamma \rightarrow \beta$, then $\alpha \rightarrow \gamma$.
  2. if $\alpha \rightarrow \beta$ and $\alpha \rightarrow \gamma$ then $\alpha \rightarrow \beta \gamma.$
  3. if $\alpha \rightarrow \beta \gamma$, then $\alpha \rightarrow \beta$ and $\alpha \rightarrow \gamma$.
  4. if $\alpha \rightarrow \beta$ and $\gamma \beta \rightarrow \delta$, then $\alpha \gamma \rightarrow \delta$.

Given the following piece of code

main()
{
    forkthem(5)
}
void forkthem(int n)
{
    if(n > 0)
    {
        fork();
        forkthem(n-1);
    }
}

How many new processes are created if the above piece of code is run?

If $\mathrm{A}$ is a set, let $|\mathrm{A}|$ denote the cardinality of set $\mathrm{A}$.

  • We say $\text{|B|}=|\text{A}|$ if and only if there exists a bijection from $\text{B}$ to $\text{A}$.
  • We say $|\mathrm{B}|<|\mathrm{A}|$ if and only if there exists an injection from $\mathrm{B}$ to $\mathrm{A}$ but there is no surjection from $\mathrm{B}$ to $\mathrm{A}$.

Which of the following is/are false?

  1. If $\text{A}$ is a proper subset of $\text{B}$, then $\text{|A|}<|\text{B}|$.
  2. The set of all infinite sequences of $0 \mathrm{s}$ and $1 \mathrm{s}$ is uncountable.
  3. If $\text{A}$ is an uncountable set then $\text{|A|}=|\text{R}|. \;(\text{R}$ is set of all real numbers)
  4. Set $\text{B}$ is infinitely countable if and only if there is a bijection $f: \text{N} \rightarrow \text{B}.\; ( \text{N}$ is set of all positive integers)

We want to use semaphores to implement a shared critical section (CS) among three threads $\text{T1, T2},$ and $\text{T3}.$ We want to enforce the execution in the CS in this order: First $\text{T2}$ must execute in the CS. When it finishes, $\text{T1}$ will then be allowed to enter the CS; and when it finishes $\text{T3}$ will then be allowed to enter the CS; when $\text{T3}$ finishes then $\text{T2}$ will be allowed to enter the CS, and so on, $(\text{T2, T1, T3, T2, T1, T3}, \ldots).$

What is the minimal number of semaphores we need in order to implement this ordering and mutual exclusion?

The result of the following addition
$$
\begin{array}{r}
11110111 \\
+11110111
\end{array}
$$
in $2\text{'s}$ complement representation on $8$ bits is:

  1. $11101110$ and the result is correct,
  2. $11101110$ but there is an overflow,
  3. $11101111$ and the result is correct
  4. $11101111$ but there is an overflow.

Let $\mathrm{G}$ and $\mathrm{H}$ be two groups with the following properties:

  1. $\text{G}$ is a group such that $\forall a,b \in \mathrm{G}\left(\left(a^* b\right)^{-1}=b^{-1} * a^{-1}\right)$
  2. $\text{H}$ is a group such that $\forall a,b \in \mathrm{H}\left(\left(a^* b\right)^{-1}=a^{-1} * b^{-1}\right) $

then which of the following is True?

  1. $\mathrm{G}$ is abelian, $\mathrm{H}$ may not be abelian.
  2. Both $\mathrm{G}$ and $\mathrm{H}$ are abelian.
  3. $\mathrm{H}$ is abelian, $\mathrm{G}$ may not be abelian.
  4. None of $\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{G}$ is necessarily abelian.

Let $\text{X}$ be a discrete random variable which is uniform over the set $\{1,2,3 \ldots n\}$ i.e, $\text{P[X}=k]=\frac{1}{n}$ for all $\mathrm{i}$ in $\{1,2,3 \ldots n\}$.

Compute $\text{E}\left[\text{X}^2\right]$

  1. $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$
  2. $\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2$
  3. $\frac{n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}$
  4. $\frac{(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}$

Which of the following decision problems is decidable$? \;\text{(TM}$ stands for Turing Machine)

  1. Given a $\text{TM M}$ and a string $w,$ does $\text{M}$ ever write the symbol $\#$ on its tape on input $y?$
  2. Given a $\text{TM M}$, are there infinitely many $\text{TMs}\; \text{M}^{\prime}$ accepting the same r.e. set $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M})?$
  3. Given a $\text{TM M}$ and a string $y,$ does $\text{M}$ accept $y?$
  4. $\{\text{M} \mid \text{$\text{TM M}$ takes more than 2023 steps on some input}\}?$

  1. $\theta(\log n)$

What will be the output printed by the following code?

Consider the following $\text{LL(1)}$ grammar.
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{S} \rightarrow \text{A} \\
& \text{A} \rightarrow \mathbf{a} \text{BE} \\
& \text{B} \rightarrow \mathbf{b} \text{CD} \\
& \text{C} \rightarrow \mathbf{c} \\
& \text{D} \rightarrow \mathbf{d} \\
& \text{E} \rightarrow \mathbf{e} \text{FG} \\
& \text{F} \rightarrow \mathbf{f} \\
& \text{G} \rightarrow \mathbf{g}
\end{aligned}
$$
In $\text{LL(1)}$ parsing, at each step in the parse the rule that must be chosen is uniquely determined by the current nonterminal and the next one lookahead symbol.

How many steps would the $\text{LL(1)}$ parser take to parse string $\textbf{abcdefg} ?$

Consider the following database schema:
$\textsf{Product (pid, name, brand, price, color), where pid}$ is the primary key.
Consider the following SQL queries:

$\textsf{Query P}:$

$\textsf{Query Q}:$

Which of the following is correct?

  1. Query $\text{P, Q}$ are equivalent.
  2. Query $\text{P, Q}$ are not equivalent But if we ignore the duplicates in the result of $\text{P, Q}$ then $\text{P, Q}$ are equivalent.
  3. Query $\text{P, Q}$ are not equivalent even if we ignore the duplicates in the result of $\text{P, Q}.$
  4. Result of query $\text{P}$ is always a superset of the result of query $\text{Q}.$

Consider the following linked list of $\textsf{ListNode}$ objects, with a pointer named front that points to the first node:
$$
\text { front } \rightarrow[1] \rightarrow[2] \rightarrow[4] \rightarrow[3] \rightarrow[5] \rightarrow[7] \rightarrow[11] \rightarrow[0] \rightarrow[6] \rightarrow[1] \rightarrow[1] \rightarrow \text{NULL}
$$
What will be the state of the linked list after the following code run on it?

void linkedListMystery(ListNode *front){
    ListNode *curr = front;
    ListNode *prev = NULL;
    while(curr → next != NULL){
        if((curr → data)%2 ==0 && prev!=NULL){
            prev → next = curr → next;
        }
        else {
            curr → data --;
        }
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr → next;
    }
}
  1. $0 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 0 \rightarrow 0 \rightarrow$ NULL
  2. $0 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 0 \rightarrow 1 \rightarrow$ NULL
  3. $0 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 0 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 0 \rightarrow$ NULL
  4. $0 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 0 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 1 \rightarrow$ NULL

Suppose a router has built up the routing table shown in the following table. The router can deliver packets directly over interfaces $0$ and $1,$ or it can forward packets to routers $\mathrm{R} 2$, $\mathrm{R} 3$, or $\text{R4}.$ Assume the router does the longest prefix match.
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline \text{Subnet Number} & \text{Subnet Mask} & \text{Next Hop} \\
\hline 128.96 .170 .0 & 255.255 .254 .0 & \text{Interface 0} \\
128.96 .168 .0 & 255.255 .254 .0 & \text{Interface 1} \\
128.96 .166 .0 & 255.255 .254 .0 & \text{R 2} \\
128.96 .164 .0 & 255.255 .252 .0 & \text{R 3} \\
\text{Default} & & \text{R4} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
What will be the next hop for a packet with destination IP address $128.96.167.151?$

  1. $\text{R2}$
  2. $\mathrm{R} 3$
  3. $\text{R4}$
  4. $\text{Interface 1}$
The number of partitions of $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ into three blocks is $25.$ The total number of functions $f:\{1,2,3,4,5\} \rightarrow\{1,2,3,4\}$ with $\mid \text{Image}(f) \mid\; =3$ is ?

For which of the following does there exist a simple undirected graph $\text{G = (V, E)}$ satisfying the specified conditions?

  1. A tree with $9$ vertices and the sum of the degrees of all the vertices is $18.$
  2. A graph with $5$ components, $12$ vertices and $7$ edges.
  3. A graph with $5$ components, $30$ vertices and $24$ edges.
  4. A graph with $9$ vertices, $9$ edges, and no cycles.

What will be the output of following program?

Assume that all necessary libraries are included.

void myfunction(char *s, char *t)
{
    int i = 0, n = 0;
    char p;
    n = strlen(s);
    while ( (p = *s) != '\0' )
    {
        t[n-i-1] = p;
        i++;
        s++;
    }
     return ;
 }
int main()
{
    char c[] = "hello";
    myfunction(c, c);
    printf("%s",c);
}
  1. $\textsf{hello}$
  2. $\textsf{heleh}$
  3. $\textsf{olleh}$
  4. $\textsf{ollel}$

Suppose that $\mathrm{X}$ is a continuous random variable such that it has the following probability density function -
$$
f(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{1}{6}, & -2 \leq x \leq 4 \\ 0, & \text { otherwise }\end{cases}
$$
Let $\text{Y}$ be a random variable defined as $\text{Y = X}^2$.

What will be $\text{P(Y} \leq 4)?$

  1. $1 / 3$
  2. $2 / 3$
  3. $1 / 6$
  4. None of these

Consider a message that is $7.5 \ast 10^6$ bits long to be sent from the source to the destination. (Assume header size is negligible relative to the entire message size). Suppose each link is $1.5$ Mbps. Focus on transmission delays only and assume all other delay components are negligible.

Suppose that the message is segmented into $5000$ packets, with each packet being $1500$ bits long. How long does it take to move the file from source host to destination host when message segmentation is used?

  1. $5.002 \mathrm{~sec}$
  2. $4.990 \mathrm{~sec}$
  3. $4.012 \mathrm{~sec}$
  4. $5.236 \mathrm{~sec}$

$\mathrm{B}^{+}-$ trees have different structures for leaf and non-leaf nodes.
In $\mathrm{B}^+-$ tree leaf node contains keys and record pointer associated with it and a block pointer pointing to the next leaf node. Non-leaf nodes contains only keys and child pointer, there is no need to store record pointer at non-leaf node, because all keys are ultimately present on leaf node.For leaf node order will be maximum number of keys, record pointer pair a node can hold, but order of non leaf node is determined by maximum child pointers it can have.

A $\mathrm{B}^+-$ tree index is to be built on the Name attribute of the relation $\text{STUDENT}.$ Assume that all student names are of length $8$ bytes, disk blocks are of size $512$ bytes, and index pointers, record pointers are of size $4$ bytes, $5$ bytes respectively. Given this scenario, the best choice for the order of leaf nodes and non-leaf nodes is $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ respectively. Then what is $\mathrm{Y}-\mathrm{X}?$

Suppose the matrix $\text{A}=\left[\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right]$ has an eigenvalue $1$ with associated eigenvector $x=\left[\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 3\end{array}\right]$. What is $A^{50} x ?$

  1. $\left[\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right]$
  2. $\left[\begin{array}{ll}a^{50} & b^{50} \\ c^{50} & d^{50}\end{array}\right]$
  3. $\left[\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 3\end{array}\right]$
  4. $\left[\begin{array}{l}2^{50} \\ 3^{50}\end{array}\right]$

Suppose that you are at a party. Any two people either have met (they are acquaintances) or have never met (they are strangers). Which of the following must be true at a party with at least two people present?
  1. There are at least two people with the same number of acquaintances at that party.
  2. There are at least two people with different numbers of acquaintances at that party.
  3. The number of people with an even number of acquaintances is even.
  4. The number of people with an odd number of acquaintances is even.

For an array $\text{A}[1 \ldots n]$, an inversion is any pair of items $\text{A}[i]$ and $\text{A}[j]$ such that $\text{A}[i] \lt \text{A}[j]$ but $i>j$.

We want to sort the input array $\text{A}[1 \ldots n]$ in the ascending order.

Which of the following is/are CORRECT?

  1. The running time of Insertion-Sort is $\Theta(n+\text{I})$, where $\text{I}$ is the number of inversions in the input array $\text{A}[1 \ldots n]$.
  2. If there are $\text{ATMOST}\; n$ inversions in the array then insertion sort takes $\theta(n)$ to sort array.
  3. If there is $\text{EXACTLY}\; 1$ inversion in the array then insertion sort takes $\theta(n)$ to sort array.
  4. If we know that there are $\operatorname{EXACTLY} \frac{\text{N}^2-\text{N}}{2}$ inversions in the array then we can sort the array in $\theta(1)$ time.

Find the limit $\displaystyle{}\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{x^2+x+1}{(3 x+2)^2}$.
  1. $1$
  2. $1 / 3$
  3. $0$
  4. $1 / 9$

Consider a file that is $1000$ disk blocks in size. Assume that a disk block is appended to the end of the file, which causes the file size to grow to $1001$ blocks. File is maintained using file descriptor which contains its metadata (like name of file, size of file etc).
Which of the following is/are correct about disk read and write operations to update the file. Assume file descriptor takes just one disk block space.

  1. In case of  Linked allocation it takes minimum $1001$ reads and $2$ writes to update the file
  2. In case of Multilevel index allocation it takes minimum $2$ reads and $3$ writes to update the file
  3. In case of  Linked allocation it takes minimum $1002$ reads and $2$ writes to update the file
  4. In case of Multilevel index allocation it takes minimum $3$ reads and $3$ writes to update the file

Consider following two states $\text{I}_j$ and $\text{I}_k$ in $\operatorname{SLR}(1)$ parsing. Here $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are non empty strings.
$$
\text{I}_k \boxed{ \begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B} \bullet \alpha \gamma \\
& \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{B} \bullet \alpha \beta
\end{aligned}}
\qquad
\text{I}_j \boxed{\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B} \bullet \alpha \gamma \\
& \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{B} \alpha \beta \bullet
\end{aligned}}
$$
Which of the following is/are TRUE?

  1. There will be Shift-Reduce conflict in $\text{I}_j$ if $\text{FIRST} (\alpha \gamma) \cap \text{FOLLOW}(c) \neq \varnothing$
  2. There will be Shift-Reduce conflict in $\text{I}_j$ if $\text{FIRST}(\alpha) \cap \text{FOLLOW}(c) \neq \varnothing$
  3. There can never be any conflict in $\text{I}_k$
  4. There is a Shift-Reduce conflict in $\text{I}_k$ if next lookhead is $\alpha$

Suppose that the system that uses $3$-level page table with $46$-bit virtual address and a $32$-bit physical address. Each level page table fits exactly in single frame. Page size is $8\;\text{KB}$ and each page table entry size is $4$ bytes. Given that the process requires $32 \mathrm{~KB}$ for code segment, $10\;\text{KB}$ for data segment and $128 \mathrm{~KB}$ for stack segment. Assume each segment is allocated with contiguous memory.
Let $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ be minimum and maximum number of frames respectively that will be occupied by multi-level page table.

What is the value of $\text{X + Y} ?$

For any language $\text{L},$ we define two operations, square and double as follows:

  • The square of a language $\mathrm{L}$ is $\mathrm{Sq}(\mathrm{L})=\{ww: w \in \mathrm{L}\};$
  • The double of a language is $\text{Do(L)}=\{w x: w, x \in \text{L}\}$.
